name: Hamming Radius
definition: The **Hamming Radius** $B(\mathcal{H})$ of a family $\mathcal{H}$ is the smallest radius of an enclosing Hamming ball, defined as $$ B(\mathcal{H}):= \min\{d: \exists T\subset \mathcal{X\},\, \forall h\in \mathcal{H},\, |h\Delta T|\le d} $$

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, being monotonic under both subfamilies and projections is doubly monotonic.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection; hence doubly monotonicity implies c-monotonicity.

monotonic.proof: Every Hamming ball containing a class also contains each of its subfamilies.

p_monotonic.proof: Projecting a containing Hamming ball gives a ball of no greater radius containing the projected class.

strict_c_monotonic.proof: Let r be the radius of $\mathcal H$, witnessed by a centre c, and let x be active. In the fibre whose fixed label differs from c(x), deleting x from c gives an enclosing ball of radius at most r-1. Hence the smaller fibre radius is below r. Also radius zero implies that all concepts equal the centre, so the class has size at most one.

strictly_monotonic.proof: Hamming radius is doubly monotonic, and the enclosing-ball argument proves strict c-monotonicity.

tight_strict_c_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: $\mathcal H=\{011,100\}$ has radius 2. Each active one-coordinate split has two singleton fibres of radius 0, whose tight recurrence value would be 1, not 2.
